# `Q-9-5` — Empty XML Document

> The XML document contains no root element.

## What this means

Every well-formed XML document has exactly one root element —
the single outermost tag that contains everything else. This
error fires when the parser reaches end-of-input without ever
seeing one: the file is empty, contains only whitespace,
contains only comments or processing instructions, or the
content that was supposed to be the root element was malformed
enough to be skipped.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **An empty file.** A zero-byte XML document.
- **A file that contains only the XML declaration**
  (`<?xml version="1.0"?>`) and no actual content.
- **A failed download** that wrote no bytes.

## How to fix

Add a root element to the document. For a CSL style, that is
`<style>...</style>`; for other XML formats, consult the
schema the document is supposed to follow.

If you did not expect the file to be empty, re-fetch it or
restore from a known-good copy.

## Related

- `Q-9-6` — multiple root elements: the opposite mistake.
- `Q-9-16` — invalid root element: a root *is* present, but it
  is not the one CSL expects.
